# Editor comments

After a round of revisions, both reviewers agree that the manuscript has greatly improved, but there are still some issues that need to be addressed by the authors.
-Rongji Mu

# Response to the Editor

We would like to thank the editor and the two reviewers for their time and careful reading of our manuscript.
We believe that their valuable feedback and the revisions we made in response have substantially improved our work.
We agree that our study compares two specific implementations of Bayesian and frequentist meta-analytic models, not the frameworks as such.
We have reframed the manuscript accordingly and have removed or narrowed the generalising claims about comparing both frameworks.
Below we respond to each point; the revised manuscript text is quoted verbatim.

# Reviewer 2


### Major comments

<!-- R2 C1 -->
:::{.comment}
Please address the omitted request for frequentist prediction intervals and Bayesian posterior predictive intervals, particularly given the very high heterogeneity and the manuscript's focus on uncertainty quantification.
:::

::: {.reply}
We have now added frequentist and Bayesian predictive intervals to the manuscript and revised the methods, results, and discussion accordingly.
We thank the reviewer for suggesting this addition and agree that it's an important addition to our manuscript.
We have also refocused the aims of our study in this direction (see also our response to reviewer 1, comment 1).
:::
